hook: The Soviet leader who ended the Cold War and let Eastern Europe go free.

pages.x: Mikhail Gorbachev was born in 1931 in Privolnoye, a village in southern Russia, to a peasant family. As a teenager he drove a combine harvester, and won a medal for a record harvest.
He studied law at Moscow University, where he met his wife Raisa, and rose through the Communist Party in his home region of Stavropol.
In 1985 he became leader of the Soviet Union, far younger than the old men before him. The economy was stuck, and the country was fighting a long war in Afghanistan.
In 1986 a nuclear reactor exploded at Chernobyl, and officials at first tried to hide it. The disaster convinced him that the country needed openness.
He brought in glasnost, openness, letting people speak and write more freely, and perestroika, a reform of the economy. Banned books were printed, and political prisoners were freed.
He met President Reagan several times, and in 1987 they signed a treaty that destroyed a whole class of nuclear missiles. He also pulled Soviet troops out of Afghanistan.
In 1989, when the peoples of Eastern Europe rose against their communist governments, he refused to send in the tanks. The Berlin Wall fell that November, and in 1990 he won the Nobel Peace Prize.

pages.t: The end of the Soviet Union
pages.x: In August 1991 hardliners held him prisoner at his holiday home in Crimea. Their coup failed within days, but the Soviet Union broke apart, and on Christmas Day 1991 he resigned.
In 1997, to raise money for his charity, he starred in a television advert for a pizza chain.
Gorbachev ended the Cold War without a war and let Eastern Europe go free, though many Russians blamed him for the collapse of their country. He died in 2022.
pts: Brought openness and reform to the Soviet Union
